name: Barak
overview: Barak is a male figure in the Book of Judges who was summoned by the prophetess Deborah to lead the Israelite forces against the army of Jabin. His role is significant in the deliverance of Israel from oppression during this period. No specific tribal affiliation or additional notes are recorded for him in the provided data.
namesAndTitles: The name Barak means 'lightning,' which may reflect the swift and decisive nature of his military leadership. Additionally, the name Bedan, meaning 'son of judgment,' is associated with him in 1 Samuel 12:11, though it is unclear if this is an alternate name or title for Barak.
familyAndRelationships: Barak is identified as the son of Abinoam, establishing a clear paternal relationship. Beyond this, Scripture does not record any other family relationships for him in the provided information.
scriptureSignificance: Barak's importance in the biblical narrative centers on his obedience to Deborah's summons to confront and defeat the Canaanite army led by Jabin. This event underscores God's use of human leaders to accomplish His purposes of deliverance and judgment against Israel's enemies. Barak's leadership, under divine direction, contributed to a pivotal moment of victory for Israel during the era of the judges.
